records.omission_quote: Previous research has suggested that women pay themselves significantly less than men pay themselves for the same amount of work (Callahan-Levy & Messé, 1979; Major, McFarlin, & Gagnon, 1984). In an experimental study involving 132 participants (68 men and 64 women), this “depressed-entitlement effect” was replicated in a current sample of university students.

records.reason: The paper directly tests whether the finding from Goldberg, Casenhiser, and White (2007)—that skewed input/order of frequent verbs facilitates construction learning—generalizes to adult L2 learners. Its reported positive comprehension result is compared with that target. The sole shipped row is Casenhiser and Goldberg (2005), a separate original.

records.identity_quote: Goldberg et al. (2007) showed that initially providing skewed input facilitated rapid construction generalization. The present study investigates this effect for the position of verbs with relative high token frequency.
